transversal|A line crossing two or more coplanar lines at distinct points.|A slanted line crosses two parallel horizontal lines.|\ell_1\parallel\ell_2|The crossing line creates angle pairs such as corresponding and alternate interior angles.

trapezoid|A quadrilateral with at least one pair of parallel sides; some courses require exactly one pair.|A trapezoid has parallel bases 5 cm and 11 cm, with height 4 cm.|A=\frac12(5+11)(4)=32\text{ cm}^2|The area formula works under either definition convention.
tree diagram|A branching display of successive choices or outcomes.|Choose tea or juice, then a small or large cup.|2\cdot2=4|The four leaves are tea-small, tea-large, juice-small, and juice-large.
trend|A general direction or pattern in data.|Weekly attendance is 22, 25, 24, 29, 31.|31-22=9|Despite one decrease, the overall trend is upward.

trend line|A line used to summarize an approximately linear pattern in a scatterplot.|A fitted model predicts score s from practice hours h.|s=6h+50|At h = 4, the trend line predicts a score of 74; individual scores may differ.
trial|One repetition of an experiment.|A student tosses a paper cup 40 times.|n=40\text{ trials}|Each toss and recorded landing is one trial.
triangle|A polygon with three sides.|Find a missing angle when the other two are 54° and 67°.|180^\circ-54^\circ-67^\circ=59^\circ|The three interior angles total 180°.

trigonometric ratios|Ratios of right-triangle side lengths associated with an acute angle.|For an angle with opposite 8, adjacent 15, and hypotenuse 17, give three ratios.|\sin\theta=\frac8{17},\quad\cos\theta=\frac{15}{17},\quad\tan\theta=\frac8{15}|Choose the side relationship for the requested ratio.
trinomial|A polynomial with exactly three nonzero terms after combining like terms.|Count the terms in x² + 6x + 8.|x^2+6x+8|The three terms make it a trinomial.
turn|An informal name for a rotation.|Turn a point (2, −5) halfway around the origin.|(2,-5)\mapsto(-2,5)|A half turn is a 180-degree rotation.

unfair game|A game giving unequal expected advantages under its rules.|Two players stake equal amounts; A wins on die faces 1–4 and B on 5–6.|P(A)=\frac46>\frac26=P(B)|With equal payouts, A has the advantage.
unit|A standard amount used to express a measurement, or one whole in a counting context.|A pencil length is recorded as 16 cm.|L=16\text{ cm}|The number is 16 and the measurement unit is centimeter.
unit fraction|A fraction with numerator 1 and a positive integer denominator.|Divide a whole into 9 equal pieces. Name one piece.|\frac19|One ninth is a unit fraction.
unit price|The cost of one item or one unit of measure.|A pack of 8 markers costs 10.40 dollars.|10.40\div8=1.30|The unit price is 1.30 dollars per marker.
unit rate|A rate expressed for one unit of its denominator quantity.|A cyclist travels 42 km in 3 hours.|42\div3=14\text{ km/h}|The unit rate is 14 kilometers per hour.

unlike denominators|Different denominators in two or more fractions.|Prepare 2/3 and 3/5 for addition.|\frac23=\frac{10}{15},\quad\frac35=\frac9{15}|The original thirds and fifths become matching fifteenths.

upper quartile|The third quartile, marking the lower edge of the highest quarter under a stated convention.|Using median-of-halves, find Q3 for 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16.|Q_3=\frac{12+14}{2}=13|The upper half is 10, 12, 14, 16; its median is 13.
variable|A symbol representing an unknown or changing quantity.|A delivery has n identical boxes weighing 6 kg each.|W=6n|The letter n represents the number of boxes.

Venn diagram|A diagram of overlapping regions used to show set relationships.|Of 20 students, 9 play chess, 8 code, and 3 do both. How many do at least one?|9+8-3=14|Subtract the overlap once so those students are not counted twice.

vertex|A meeting point of sides, edges, or rays; a parabola's turning point also has this name.|Name the vertex of angle RST.|\angle RST\quad\Rightarrow\quad S|The shared endpoint is the middle letter.
vertical angles|Opposite angles formed by two intersecting lines.|One angle at an intersection measures 73°. Find its vertically opposite angle.|\theta=73^\circ|Vertical angles have equal measures.
vertical axis|The up-and-down reference axis of a graph, usually the y-axis.|A point lies on the vertical axis with height −6.|P=(0,-6)|Every point on the y-axis has x-coordinate zero.

volume|The amount of three-dimensional space occupied or enclosed, measured in cubic units.|A box is 4 cm wide, 5 cm deep, and 7 cm tall.|V=4(5)(7)=140\text{ cm}^3|Multiply all three dimensions to count unit cubes.

weight|The force of gravity on an object, often reported in customary weight units in everyday contexts.|A parcel's reported weight is 2 pounds 8 ounces. Express it in ounces.|2(16)+8=40\text{ oz}|Convert pounds to ounces before adding.
whole number|One of 0, 1, 2, 3, and so on.|Which of −2, 0, 3/2, and 7 are whole numbers?|\{0,7\}|Whole numbers include zero but exclude negative integers and noninteger fractions.
word form|Writing a number using words rather than digits.|Write 3,408 in words.|3408|The word form is 'three thousand four hundred eight'.
x-axis|The horizontal axis in the usual coordinate plane.|Find where a point on the x-axis can have a nonzero coordinate.|P=(7,0)|All points on the x-axis have y-coordinate zero.
x-coordinate|The first coordinate in an ordered pair, measuring horizontal position.|Read the horizontal coordinate of (−8, 3).|x=-8|The point is eight units left of the origin.
x-intercept|A point where a graph crosses or touches the x-axis; also the x-value of that point.|Find the x-intercept of y = 3x − 12.|0=3x-12\quad\Rightarrow\quad x=4|The intercept point is (4, 0).
y-axis|The vertical axis in the usual coordinate plane.|Give a point five units above the origin on the y-axis.|P=(0,5)|Every point on this axis has x-coordinate zero.
y-coordinate|The second coordinate in an ordered pair, measuring vertical position.|Read the vertical coordinate of (6, −9).|y=-9|The point is nine units below the x-axis.
y-intercept|A point where a graph crosses or touches the y-axis; also its y-value.|Find the y-intercept of y = −2x + 7.|x=0\quad\Rightarrow\quad y=7|The intercept point is (0, 7).
yard|A customary length unit equal to three feet or thirty-six inches.|Convert 2.5 yards to feet.|2.5(3)=7.5\text{ ft}|Multiply yards by 3.
zero pair|Two opposite quantities or counters that combine to zero.|Pair one +1 counter with one −1 counter.|1+(-1)=0|Adding or removing a zero pair does not change the total value.
Zero Property of Addition|Adding zero leaves a number unchanged; also called the additive identity property.|A score of −16 receives no change.|-16+0=-16|Zero is the identity for addition.
